NODE LAYER: FROM/TO are integer endpoint nodes; an endpoint may occur on several elements and physical branches. Changing a logical node or its aliases must consider the full incident graph; element ordinal or same branch label does not establish source-target engineering identity.

POINTER LAYER: nonzero ELEMENTS auxiliary pointer references an indexed record in its own section; pointer 0 means no auxiliary record. Check section presence, bounds, index base, pointer-to-owner multiplicity and record type; never use a pointer as a node number.

RIGID LAYER: auxiliary pointer #2 points to #$ RIGID (Rigid Weight/Type), not a node-level field. Pointer=0 means unattached and differs from attached weight=0. Shared/invalid targets require atomicity or HOLD; Rigid Type code definitions must be source-checked.

NODENAME LAYER: ELEMENTS pointer #12 addresses #$ NODENAME record with physical FROM/TO alias slots. A single logical node can have several aliases across B2/B4; complete closure required. Existing VNext normal-node-closure remains protected.

NUMERIC / SENTINEL LAYER: real zero, absent pointer 0, 9999.99, -1, signed zero, near-zero 1E-10, blank labels and scientific/D-exponent text have different field-context meanings. Units/width/range/precision are field-specific; never globally coerce values.
